newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore's Goh says saddened by Deng's death.
newsitem.headline: Singapore's Goh says saddened by Deng's death.

text.p: Singapore Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong said on Thursday he was saddened by the death of Deng Xiaoping, but said the legacy of the paramount leader would be a "strong and prosperous China".
"I am saddened to learn of Deng Xiaoping's demise," Goh said in a statement.
Goh, who met Deng several times, described him as one the world's great leaders who "saw events in historical sweep, and thought in terms of generations".
"He brought about the greatest economic revolution in history, involving not just one billion people in China, but also affecting the lives of others in Asia."
Deng had meticulously planned the leadership succession and China's present leaders shared his vision, Goh said. "Deng's legacy will be a strong and prosperous China in the 21st Century," he added.
Deng died late on Wednesday from respiratory failure. He was 92.
The government's Economic Development Board (EDB) said it was confident investments in China would keep growing despite Deng's death.
"The EDB is confident that investments between China and Singapore will continue to grow," the EDB said in a written reply to a query from Reuters.

"As part of its on-going efforts to participate in the tremendous growth in the Asia Pacific, the EDB, through its regionalisation programme, will continue to assist companies to venture into China and the region," the statement said.

The EDB said Singapore was the fifth largest investor in China, with total investment amounting to US$1.86 billion in 1995. Singapore companies invested a further $987 million in China in the first six months of 1996, it said.
EDB is a government body formed to seek foreign investments at home and encourage local companies to venture abroad.
